summary: ObsDriveBench is a multiple-choice benchmark for vision-language models in autonomous driving under adverse weather. It is built from K-Radar camera/LiDAR/radar frames (over 1.4k training and 1.3k test frames, giving more than 14k training and 13k test questions) and covers observability awareness, spatial reliability, and risk-aware decision-making. The authors also train ObsDrive (Qwen2.5VL-7B with SFT on normal weather, then GRPO on adverse weather) and report gains over 14 off-the-shelf models.

claims.claim: Existing VLMs degrade consistently under real adverse weather and show modality bias (camera > LiDAR > radar).
claims.evidence: §5.2.2 / Table 2: qualitative description of degradation across rain, snow, sleet, and fog and per modality; 14 off-the-shelf models in Table 1.

claims.claim: ObsDrive (SFT + adverse-weather RL) improves robustness across all three capabilities and transfers cross-dataset.
claims.evidence: §5.2.2 (Ours-RL > Ours-SFT); §5.4: beats Qwen2.5-VL-7B in all 20 DriveBench task-condition settings (Table 4) and by 0.93/0.36 (night) and 1.22/0.72 (rain) on DriveLMM-o1 (Table 5). Compared mainly against its own base model; no variance reported; answers scored with an LLM judge.

patterns.note: GRPO fine-tuning of a VLM for driving perception; not an agent harness and not software engineering.

methodology.sample: K-Radar-derived frames; over 14k training and 13k test MCQs.
methodology.baselines: 14 off-the-shelf MLLMs including GPT-5, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Qwen-VL, InternVL, driving-specific models.
methodology.contamination_controls: Off-the-shelf models not trained on the ObsDriveBench training split (§5.1).

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; no venue in comment.
standards.artifacts: Dataset and evaluation code 'will be released' (github.com/russellyq/ObsDriveBench per abstract).

biases.detail: Autonomous-driving multimodal perception; unrelated to LLM coding agents or software engineering harnesses.
MCQ answer correctness judged with an LLM-as-judge (§5.1) without a reported validation.

coi.affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CSE; Institute of Medical Intelligence and XR).
coi.funding: No acknowledgments or funding section found.
coi.detail: Academic benchmark. The authors also ship the top-ranked baseline (ObsDrive), but there is no commercial interest.

verdict_reason: Off-topic: an autonomous-driving vision-language benchmark under adverse weather, with no bearing on LLM coding agents, agent harnesses, or software engineering.
applicability: Does not transfer. Nothing here informs a reference team building an agentic harness for the domain cross-repository work across several repositories, mixed agent hosts, or spec-driven development.
